scope: Corollary 5.2 of the manuscript “The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis via elementary expansions” (preprints/The-Grothendieck-homotopy-hypothesis-via-elementary-expansions-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 312 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 489bb8f5a448c3fc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 24-25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every Grothendieck coherator C, the canonical semi-model category Mod(C) is Quillen equivalent to spaces. More precisely, there is a geometric-realization/fundamental- infinity-groupoid adjunction | − | : Mod(C) ⇄ Spaces : Π∞ 24 which is a Quillen equivalence. In particular, Mod(C)[W−1 ] ≃ Ho(Spaces). Thus the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis holds for these groupoids.
